title: The Lingering Shadow of Rodrigo Duterte’s Drug War in the Philippines
author: Aubin Eymard
text:
Salvacion Ramos (left) and Llore Pasco (right) have remained in close contact every week since the deaths of their respective children, and are fighting for justice.
Credit: Aubin Eymard
A few bags of chips and sweets line the modest storefront of Salvacion Ramos’ home in the Batasan neighborhood on the outskirts of Manila. At 68, she has turned the front of her house into a small convenience store to help pay for the education of her grandson, who has been in her care since her daughter’s death.It was on that same doorstep one night in February 2017 that Cristeta Ramos was shot once in the back and three times in the head by four plainclothes police officers. “She died in my arms. I didn’t even get to say goodbye,” Salvacion recalls, tears in her eyes.[...]
